bio_en: Vahan Kardashian was born in Caesarea on 1 December 1883; his mother and sister died on the deportation roads in 1915. He emigrated to New York in 1902, graduated in law in 1908 and opened a law office in 1909. Until 1914 he was legal counsel to the Ottoman embassy in Washington and consulate in New York, and in 1913 went to Constantinople to negotiate a large American loan. After the deportations he became one of the most passionate defenders of the Armenian Cause in America, waging a long campaign against Charles Hughes's policy, and died of heart disease in New York on 9 June 1934.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: high. Advocate rather than fighter.
